lines.text: When a Category 5 hurricane slams into the coast, what actually causes the most catastrophic damage?
Most people fear the one hundred and fifty mile per hour winds, but wind isn't the primary killer.
The storm's central low pressure and violent winds act like a giant bulldozer pushing the ocean forward.
This creates a massive wall of seawater called a storm surge, rising over twenty feet above sea level.
A single cubic yard of water weighs nearly one ton, easily demolishing brick homes and concrete bridges.
Once over land, the hurricane loses warm ocean fuel, weakening into torrential inland rain deluges.
Storm surge causes nearly ninety percent of all direct hurricane fatalities.
